text:
jia: Hey team — noticed sustained tail latency spikes on Dedicated GPU pools when the evictor goes into a "windup" state (lots of scans then a big push). Seems cross-tenant: one noisy tenant triggers long stalls for others.

marta: Ugh. Seen that in perf dash too. Spikes line up with large batched offloads + compaction runs.

omar: Can you paste the timeline / logs?

jia: Yeah. Snip: 
```
[12:23:03] evictor: scan start tenant=accel-42 candidates=12456
[12:23:04] evictor: compaction start slab=bigpage pool=host-staging
[12:23:08] evictor: offload batch size=8192 latency_ms=6200
[12:23:12] runtime: rpc stall detected tenant=accel-17 duration_ms=4800
```

sam: So the problem is the evictor "windup" doing large contiguous work without yielding. We saw similar in other allocators but per-tenant fairness wasn't enforced.

marta: Proposal A: per-tenant eviction budget + cooperative yields. Evictor charges budget for scan/compaction/offload and yields when exhausted. Budgets refill smoothly.

omar: Proposal B: soft-throttle windup based on observed downstream RPC latency. If RPC latency > threshold, throttle eviction loops to small quanta and push work to background threads with lower IO priority.

jia: Both sound reasonable. Tradeoffs: A guarantees fairness but adds bookkeeping; B reacts to symptoms and might be late. Also B needs tight, low-noise latency signal.

sam: Agreed. Also need to avoid pathological cases: a tenant with lots of short-lived allocations could get starved if we enforce simple slotting. Maybe use a leaky-bucket style budget: refill rate proportional to tenant weight and min reserve for critical tenants.

marta: Implementation sketch:
```
struct TenantEvictState {
  int64_t budget_tokens; // microseconds of eviction work
  double refill_rate; // tokens/sec
  int priority_class; // 0..3
}
// evict loop:
while (candidates) {
  if (tenant.budget_tokens < cost_hint) yield();
  do_work(cost_hint);
  tenant.budget_tokens -= cost_hint;
}
```

omar: Metrics we must add: per-tenant evict_ms, per-tenant offload_bytes, evict loop preemptions, and a realtime RPC-latency correlation metric. Need dashboards + alert if preemptions > X and RPC-latency delta > Y.

jia: Ops question: default weights? For Dedicated customers we should preserve SLAs so maybe expose tenant.weight in control plane and allow operator overrides. For Hosted multi-tenant pools default to equal-share but special-case 'system' and infra tenants.

sam: Also consider "evict preemption" hook in allocator: when preempted, try to convert large compaction to smaller in-place frees or postpone compaction to off-peak. That reduces IO bursts.

marta: Backward compatibility: keep existing evict policy flags but add `evict.fairness=enabled|disabled`. Rollout plan: turn on in a canary pool first (1 GPU), monitor preemption metrics and tail latency for 48–72h.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout triggered for evict-fairness v1 -> pool:dedicated-canary-3 at 2026-03-20T14:05:00Z by @marta

omar: For next steps I'll prototype tenant budget state in the allocator and wire the token accounting. Jia, can you own dashboards/alerts?

jia: Yep. I'll add the metrics and a dashboard. Also will create a short e2e test that simulates noisy tenant + small-tenant RPCs.

sam: I'll draft a tiny RFC with the API surface (control-plane weight, runtime flags, metrics) and include perf numbers from the canary.

marta: Great. If we keep the initial implementation conservative (low default refill) we should avoid regressions. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
